failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector used the ratio (recent-half median effort)/(early-half median effort). A leak drives the affected loop to its 12 V saturation, so after a few windows both medians equal 12 V and the ratio collapses to ~1.0; the flag then never fires. All five fault scenarios consequently missed 196-251 s per leaking tank (missed*300 dominates the score) while the quiet ratio test still produced zero false positives.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the per-tank absolute effort-ceiling test plus the non-decreasing-error guard, and leave setpoints at nominal so the tank1/tank2 cross-coupling cannot manufacture false positives via setpoint moves; re-validate on held-out fault timings.

self_check: tank1 fires only if max(recent 10 pump_effort) >= 10.75 V AND recent-half mean|error| > 0.04 AND error not falling by >0.03. Healthy fault-free max effort is 10.59 V (start-up) and 10.54 V (settled), both < 10.75, so the high start-up mean|error| of 0.1262 (settled 0.0154) cannot trigger it. tank2 threshold 10.0 V vs healthy max 8.76 V (start-up)/9.26 V (settled), mean|error| 0.1091/0.0202 also harmless. The effort ceiling, not the error floor, separates faults from the start-up transient.
proposed_change: Replace the saturating ratio test with per-tank absolute effort ceilings (10.75 V tank1, 10.0 V tank2) combined with an error floor and a non-decreasing-error guard. Hold both setpoints at their nominal values (only restoring drift toward nominal) to avoid cross-coupling false positives.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Detection used ratio(recent effort / baseline effort) > 1.8 AND mean|error| > 0.03. During the start-up transient the baseline effort is already high and ramping (loop1 up to 10.59 V, loop2 up to 8.76 V), so the 10 s ratio stays near 1 even when a leaking tank's regulating loop rails at the 12 V pump limit; the detector therefore never fired, and every second of every leak was scored as a miss on that tank (200-251 s per fault scenario x 300). The error term did not help because healthy start-up mean|error| (0.126 m tank1, 0.109 m tank2) overlaps the fault values.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Re-test the absolute-rail detector on the held-out battery; if any healthy settled loop2 effort approaches the 9.8 V threshold, widen the margin and re-verify release timing on transient (start/stop) leaks.

self_check: tank1 fault test = max(tank1.pump_effort over last 5 samples) > 11.0 V; fault-free reference never exceeds 10.59 V (start-up range [4.15,10.59]) or 10.54 V (settled range [8.79,10.54]), i.e. >=0.4 V margin. tank2 fault test = max(tank2.pump_effort over last 5 samples) > 9.8 V; fault-free reference max is 8.76 V (start-up [6.08,8.76]) and 9.26 V (settled [8.52,9.26]), i.e. >=0.54 V margin. Leaks rail the loop at 12.0 V in the traces, well clear of both thresholds. Release gate = level rise over the last 10 s > 0.015 m; healthy settled level slope is ~0.000 m/10 s, active-leak plateau ~0.001 m/10 s, while post-fault recovery is ~0.038-0.043 m/10 s. Error is deliberately NOT thresholded because healthy start-up mean|error| (0.126 m tank1, 0.109 m tank2, ranges up to 0.156/0.153 m) overlaps fault error, which is exactly what made the old detector fire-miss and would make an error threshold false-positive during start-up.
proposed_change: Replace the ratio-of-effort test with an absolute pump-rail test: flag a tank when its own loop effort (the off-diagonally paired pump) exceeds the highest effort ever seen fault-free, and release only when the tank's level has actually climbed (>15 mm per 10 s), since the loop stays railed while it refills. Setpoints are lowered by a small step only while flagged (floor nominal-0.05, which keeps the loop railed and cannot de-saturate a mild leak) and stepped back to nominal when the flag clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector compared recent effort to a 'baseline' taken from the FIRST half of the same 50-sample window. Because the window always ends at the call time, once a leak has been present for more than ~25 s the baseline is already faulted, so ratio = recent/baseline collapses to ~1.0 and the flag never fires (traces show effort pinned at 12.0 V with ratio << 1.8). The 0.03 error floor is far too low (healthy settled mean|error| is 0.0154-0.0202), so the whole detector is both blind to real faults and mis-tuned against noise.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Re-anchor detection on ABSOLUTE physical limits (pump saturation at 12 V, healthy effort ceiling 10.6 V, level slope) instead of self-referential ratios, then tune the post-fault-clear release to cut the ~20 s of held false positives.

self_check: Thresholds vs measured healthy reference. (1) Saturation: mean(effort[-10:]) >= 11.0 V. Healthy tank1 effort max = 10.59 V (start-up t=1-199) and 10.54 V (settled t>=200); healthy tank2 max = 8.76 V (start-up) and 9.26 V (settled). Margins: 0.41 V for tank1, >=1.74 V for tank2 -> no healthy sample can reach 11.0 V. (2) Falling-level: (mean(level[-20:-10]) - mean(level[-10:])) > 0.012 m AND mean(effort[-10:]) >= 9.5 V. Healthy level is monotonically rising through start-up (error 0.1558 -> 0.0743, i.e. drop strongly NEGATIVE) and in settled operation oscillation amplitude is < 0.007 m (error range [-0.0062, 0.0736] for tank1, [0.0019, 0.0495] for tank2), far below the 0.012 m drop threshold. (3) Big-error: mean(|error[-10:]|) > 0.10 AND mean(effort[-10:]) >= 10.0 V AND level not falling-free (drop > -0.004 m). Healthy settled mean|error| = 0.0154 (t1) / 0.0202 (t2), max 0.0736 m < 0.10; healthy start-up mean|error| reaches 0.1262 but the level is RISING (drop ~ -0.05 m), so the drop > -0.004 gate excludes it. All three healthy regimes give flags = False on both tanks.
proposed_change: Replace the self-referential effort-ratio test with three absolute, physics-grounded conditions: pump saturation (effort >= 11 V, healthy ceiling 10.6 V), a confirmed 10-s level drop > 12 mm with elevated effort, and a large sustained error (> 0.10 m) with non-recovering level. Lower a tank's setpoint only while its fault is detected (never below level + 0.05 m, so the loop stays driven and no sign flip / safety violation can occur) and step it back toward nominal as soon as the fault clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The anomaly test compares the recent-half median loop effort to the first-half median of the SAME 50 s window. When a leak persists, both halves of the window are already saturated at 12 V, so the ratio is ~1.0 and the condition never fires, while the |error| gate cannot separate a fault from the healthy start-up (their errors overlap). Result: the flags stay off for essentially the entire leak, producing ~250 missed seconds per leaking tank; tank1_leak/tank2_leak/both_leaks/severe scenarios all collapse to IAE + missed*300.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the within-window ratio test with an absolute effort-saturation test using the measured healthy effort ranges (tank1 loop max 10.59 V, tank2 loop max 9.26 V), gated by a short-horizon level-slope check so the flag drops during a cleared leak's fast recovery; do not use error as a discriminator because start-up mean|e| already exceeds any usable gate.

self_check: EFF_FAST=11.2 V and EFF_MED=10.9 V (median of last 20 effort samples) vs measured HEALTHY effort: tank1 loop (pump2) start-up range [4.15,10.59] V, settled [8.79,10.54] V -> margins of 0.61 V / 0.31-0.66 V and zero baseline activations; tank2 loop (pump1) start-up [6.08,8.76] V, settled [8.52,9.26] V -> margins >1.9 V. Under fault the corresponding loop pins at 12.0 V, so both thresholds are crossed with big margin. RECOVERY_SLOPE=0.0015 m/s on the last 10 samples: measured post-clear recovery slope ~0.0027-0.0047 m/s (correctly excluded), sustained-fault drift ~0.0005 m/s (still flagged). Error is deliberately NOT gated: healthy start-up mean|e| = 0.126 (tank1) and 0.109 (tank2) overlap fault errors (e.g. 0.25), so any error threshold that catches faults would false-positive during start-up. No setpoint moves are made, so restore_gap = 0 and no new violation risk.
proposed_change: Detect each tank's leak from its own loop's absolute effort saturation (fast max>11.2 V over 8 samples, or median>10.9 V over 20 samples), which is immune to the sustained-fault blindness of the old within-window ratio and does not false-fire on the cross-coupled healthy loop. Gate the flag off only while the level is climbing faster than 0.0015 m/s (post-clear recovery), keep setpoints at nominal, and raise no flags when effort stays in the measured healthy bands.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor uses fixed effort thresholds that are too low, causing false positives during recovery and missed detections during early fault onset, especially in tank2_leak and both_leaks scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Consider adaptive thresholds based on recent error levels and level slope to better distinguish faults from normal transients and recovery.

self_check: Tank1: EFF_HIGH=11.0 vs healthy max effort 10.59 (start-up) and 10.54 (settled); EFF_MED=10.0 vs 10.59/10.54 but with ERR_MED=0.08 > settled max error 0.0736 and slope guard. Tank2: EFF_HIGH=10.0 vs healthy max effort 8.76 (start-up) and 9.26 (settled); EFF_MED=8.9 vs 8.76/9.26 but with ERR_MED=0.06 > settled max error 0.0495 and slope guard. Start-up max errors (0.1558, 0.1531) exceed ERR_MED but are protected by positive level slope.
proposed_change: Replace effort-only detection with a multi-condition approach using effort magnitude, level slope, error magnitude, and sudden effort jumps, with per-tank thresholds derived from healthy reference statistics.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Effort-only threshold with EFF_FAST=11.2 delays detection of mild leaks, and no recovery guard lets false positives persist when a cleared leak leaves the tank's own loop effort elevated during level recovery (e.g., tank1 at t=580 in tank2_leak).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add per-tank error-slope early trigger and a recovery guard that suppresses the flag when error is positive and decreasing, and lower effort thresholds to per-tank healthy maxima.

self_check: tank1 healthy effort max: start-up 10.59 V, settled 10.54 V; threshold 10.8 V. tank2 healthy effort max: start-up 8.76 V, settled 9.26 V; threshold 9.8 V. Early trigger requires error slope >0.002 m/s and error >0.04 m; healthy start-up errors are decreasing (negative slope) and settled errors are <0.05 m (tank1 max 0.0736 but not increasing rapidly). Recovery guard uses error slope < -0.00005 m/s, which healthy ranges do not satisfy when effort is high.
proposed_change: Replace single effort-threshold test with per-tank effort thresholds (10.8 V tank1, 9.8 V tank2) plus an early error-slope trigger (>0.002 m/s with error>0.04 m) to catch faults before full saturation. Add a recovery guard that suppresses the flag when error is positive and decreasing (slope < -0.00005 m/s), eliminating false positives during post-clear level recovery.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Current supervisor uses effort thresholds (11.2/10.9 V) with a weak slope guard; it misses early leaks because loop effort ramps slowly, and false-positives on the non-leaking tank during cross-coupled recovery when its effort transiently exceeds 10.9 V.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Validate the two-tier error-delta detector on a held-out battery with varying leak magnitudes and timings.

self_check: tank1: EFF_HIGH=11.0 V > healthy max 10.59 V (start-up) and 10.54 V (settled); ERR_HIGH=0.08 m, but condition requires delta_err>0.005 m/10 s, so start-up healthy max error 0.1558 m with decreasing error does not trigger. tank2: EFF_HIGH=9.8 V > healthy max 9.26 V; EFF_LOW=8.0 V; ERR_HIGH=0.06 m > settled max 0.0495 m, and start-up max 0.1531 m occurs with decreasing error, so no false positive.
proposed_change: Replace effort-only detection with a per-tank two-tier rule: high effort (tank1>11.0 V, tank2>9.8 V) with non-recovering error, or moderate effort (tank1>9.5 V, tank2>8.0 V) with error increase >5 mm/10 s and error above 0.08/0.06 m. Return nominal setpoints unchanged.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Detection relies only on absolute pump effort thresholds, causing late flags when a leak's level drops before effort rises, and false positives when effort stays high during recovery or cross-coupled disturbance.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Add level-slope based onset detection and recovery release; validate against held-out battery.

self_check: Thresholds: level-drop slope < -0.0015 m/s with error > 0.03 and level < sp-0.02; effort >= 10.7 V (tank1) or 10.0 V (tank2) with error > 0.05 and slope <= 0.0003; saturation >= 11.8 V with slope < 0.0015. Healthy startup: tank1 max effort 10.59 < 10.7, tank2 max 8.76 < 10.0; healthy settled: tank1 max effort 10.54 < 10.7, tank2 max 9.26 < 10.0; max errors 0.1558/0.1531 startup, 0.0736/0.0495 settled. No healthy condition meets thresholds.
proposed_change: Add level-drop onset detector and slope-gated effort/saturation conditions to flag leaks early and release during recovery; keep setpoints nominal.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The two worst scenarios (both_leaks, tank1_leak) are dominated by missed-anomaly and false-positive seconds, not by threshold choice: because flags are held for a full 10 s call period, a leak onset at t and the next call at t+10 inherently costs up to 10 missed seconds, and a leak clearing mid-interval inherently costs up to 10 false-positive seconds. The current thresholds (tank1 10.7 V vs healthy max 10.59 V/10.54 V; tank2 10.0 V vs 8.76 V/9.26 V) sit only 0.11-0.16 V above the largest healthy effort on tank1, which is a fragile margin for unseen episodes, and the supervisor never uses its setpoint authority, so the IAE term of every fault scenario is left on the table.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the combined drop-or-saturation detector but validate the saturation-gated setpoint mitigation on the held-out battery, and re-check that the recovery guard (slope > +0.8 mm/s) never suppresses a genuine slow-onset leak whose level has briefly plateaued.

self_check: Effort thresholds: tank1 11.0 V vs healthy maxima 10.59 V (start-up, t=1-199) and 10.54 V (settled, t>=200) -> 0.41 V margin; tank2 9.7 V vs 8.76 V and 9.26 V -> 0.44 V margin. Drop test requires slope < -1.5 mm/s AND error-vs-nominal > 40 mm AND level > 20 mm below nominal; healthy slopes after t=50 are roughly 0 to -0.5 mm/s (the t=50 dip is about -0.1 mm/s between 0.145 and 0.144 m) while leak onset shows -4 to -5 mm/s with 0.13-0.22 m error. Recovery guard: slope > +0.8 mm/s forces the flag off; the post-leak rise is about +4 mm/s (tank1 0.062 m at t=400 to 0.143 m at t=420), so recovery flags clear at the first call. Saturation test also needs error-vs-nominal > 50 mm, above the 15.4 mm mean / 73.6 mm peak healthy settled error only when paired with the effort and non-rising-slope conditions.
proposed_change: Combine a level-drop test (slope < -1.5 mm/s with >40 mm error measured against the nominal target) with a slope-gated saturation test (effort above 11.0 V for tank1 and 9.7 V for tank2) so onset is caught at the first call and recovery is suppressed whenever the level is clearly rising. When a tank is flagged and its loop is saturated, lower that tank's setpoint to level+0.06 m (clamped to 0.05-0.48 m), and return the nominal setpoint the moment the flag clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current detector relies on effort thresholds that fire late during leak onset and stay high during recovery, causing missed anomalies and false positives; it also lacks a slope-based recovery guard.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Once detection is solid, consider lowering setpoints only for persistent faults to reduce IAE, with a separate recovery detection to avoid missed anomalies.

self_check: Thresholds: tank1 EFF_HI=10.8 V vs healthy settled max 10.54 V and start-up max 10.59 V; tank2 EFF_HI=9.5 V vs healthy settled max 9.26 V and start-up max 8.76 V. ERR_HIGH=0.05 m vs healthy settled error max tank1 0.0736 m, tank2 0.0495 m. Early drop requires slope < -0.001 m/s and err > 0.04 m; start-up slopes are positive. High-effort requires slope <= 0.0005 m/s, so recovery (rising level) is ignored. 1.5x leaks yield tank1 err≈0.06 m, tank2 err≈0.09 m, both above ERR_HIGH.
proposed_change: Replace effort-only detection with a combined high-effort and early-drop condition using nominal-target error, level slope, and effort thresholds set above healthy maxima. Keep setpoints at nominal to avoid restore-gap risk while eliminating missed onsets and recovery false positives.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor sets anomaly flags correctly at the first call after a fault starts, so missed counts (8 for tank1, 4 for tank2) are minimal and stem from the 10 s flag hold. However, after a leak clears, the loose recovery slope thresholds (RECOV_SLOPE=0.0003, SAT_RECOV=0.0015) keep the flag high for several seconds, causing false positives (up to 9 per tank in both_leaks). The cross-coupling signature—leaking tank's loop effort saturating while the other loop's effort drops—is already captured by the effort thresholds, but recovery clearing is too slow.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Lower the recovery slope thresholds to clear the flag as soon as the level starts rising; keep setpoints at nominal to avoid increasing IAE against nominal targets.

self_check: For tank1, healthy start-up effort max = 10.59 V < EFF_HI=10.7 V; settled max = 10.54 V < 10.7 V. SAT_EFF=11.8 V is above all healthy efforts. For tank2, start-up max = 8.76 V < EFF_HI=10.0 V; settled max = 9.26 V < 10.0 V. SAT_EFF=11.8 V is above all healthy efforts. Recovery slope thresholds (0.0002 m/s) only apply when effort >= 10.7 V (tank1) or >= 10.0 V (tank2), which never occurs in the reference healthy ranges, so no false positives are introduced. During a persistent leak, level slope is ~0, so the flag remains; after a leak clears, slope becomes positive (>0.0002 m/s), clearing the flag earlier.
proposed_change: Lower RECOV_SLOPE and SAT_RECOV from 0.0003/0.0015 to 0.0002 so the anomaly flag clears as soon as the leaky tank's level starts rising. This reduces false positives after fault clearing without increasing missed detections at onset.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The worst scenarios (both_leaks 6142, tank1_leak 3643) are dominated by missed and false-positive counts, not IAE. Because the leaking tank's own loop saturates at 12 V, the ~10 s call latency makes ~8 s of onset miss unavoidable, but the post-clear call still sees a non-positive 10 s slope and holds the saturation flag on, producing 5-9 s of false positives per tank; the held-flag design converts each mistimed call into up to 10 s of error.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the saturation-plus-fast-recovery rule; only re-tune thresholds if a held-out scenario regresses by more than the tolerance, and never reintroduce effort-only thresholds. Verify on a held-out battery before promoting.

self_check: Effort saturation: tank1 threshold 11.0 V vs healthy max 10.59 V (start-up) and 10.54 V (settled); tank2 threshold 9.7 V vs healthy max 8.76 V (start-up) and 9.26 V (settled). Fast-drop: slope over last 5 samples <= -0.0025 m/s (=15 mm/5 s fall) AND err>0.03 m AND level<sp-0.02 m; healthy start-up error is +0.0743..+0.1558 (tank1) and +0.0499..+0.1531 (tank2) with rising level (positive slope), settled error is -0.0062..+0.0736 (tank1) and +0.0019..+0.0495 (tank2), so no qualifying 15 mm/5 s fall occurs. Slow-drop: slope over last 10 samples <= -0.0018 m/s (=18 mm/10 s) AND err>0.05 m AND level<sp-0.03 m. Recovery override: slope over last 5 samples >= +0.0030 m/s (15 mm/5 s rise) suppresses any flag, which healthy data never shows while a fault persists.
proposed_change: Add a 5-sample slope that both triggers a fast-drop flag before the loop saturates and overrides any saturation flag once the tank rises >=15 mm in 5 s, so a cleared leak stops being reported. Keep setpoints at nominal to avoid restore-gap and guarantee no new safety violation.
